transcript.text: Samsung RS68A8820S9/EU flashing 22E on the display and the fridge side isn't as cold as it should be. What does 22E mean and can I fix it?

The code 22E on Samsung fridge-freezers typically indicates a fault with the evaporator fan in the fridge section. This is the fan that circulates cold air from the freezer into the fridge; if it stops working or gets blocked by ice, the fridge side will become warm while the error flashes. You can often fix this yourself if it’s caused by an ice blockage (which might happen after a power cut or if the door was left ajar). However, if the fan motor itself has failed, it will need replacing. To determine which it is: is the freezer compartment still freezing properly (ice cream solid, ice cubes hard), or has it gone warm too?
The freezer side is fine, still frozen solid and the ice maker and dispenser work. It's just the fridge side that's warm, about 9C, with very weak airflow from the vents.

The 22E code on your Samsung suggests there is an issue with the fridge evaporator fan or airflow. This is usually caused by a defrost system fault where ice builds up over time. You can fix this yourself if it's just an ice blockage. Please perform a full manual defrost: switch the appliance off at the wall socket, remove all food (using cool bags/towels), and leave both doors open for 24 hours to ensure all internal ice melts. Dry everything thoroughly, plug it back in, and check if cooling returns to normal after a few hours. If the fridge cools down normally but the error/ice returns within a few days, the defrost system (heater or thermostat) has failed and will need an engineer to replace the part.

I've done the full defrost with the doors open and the code cleared and the fridge cooled down. But 22E came back about 10 days later, so it looks like the ice is returning. There's no burning smell or tripping, by the way. What does that mean for the repair?

The ice is building up again because the appliance isn't melting it off during its normal operation. This points to a fault in the defrost system itself—most commonly the defrost heater has burned out or the defrost thermostat/sensor has failed. These are sealed-system electrical components that need replacing by an engineer; they cannot be fixed by the user. Before calling one, please check if the drain hole at the bottom of the back wall inside the fridge is clear. If it's blocked with debris, clearing it might help, but given the recurring error, a part replacement is highly likely needed.

I can look, but I'm not sure which hole you mean. I can't remove the inner back panel and won't try. I can see a bit of frost around the vent at the top back of the fridge. Is there anything else I can check, or should I get an engineer?

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. Given the ice is returning after a full defrost and you cannot safely remove the back panel to check the drain, this suggests a fault in the automatic defrost system—most likely the defrost heater has burned out or the thermostat has failed. These are sealed electrical components that require an engineer to replace. Please book a repair; do not attempt to force the panels off as this can damage the unit.
